newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Arabs scuffle with Israel army in Hebron, Jericho.
newsitem.headline: Arabs scuffle with Israel army in Hebron, Jericho.

text.p: Palestinians clashed with Israeli forces on Tuesday at two sites in the occupied West Bank.
In the city of Hebron, Palestinians scuffled with Israeli troops who prevented about 1,500 students from entering Hebron University, which Israel shut in March.

Students were enraged by what they said was Israel reneging on a promise to reopen the university, shut after a wave of Islamist suicide attacks inside Israel killed 59 people last February and March.

In the Jordan Valley near Jericho, Palestinian Agriculture Minister Abdel-Jawwad Saleh led 100 Arabs in a protest against attempts by Jewish settlers to plough lands controlled by the Israeli military that the PLO says should fall under Palestinian self-rule.
Witnesses said protesters clashed with Israeli soldiers who tried to evict them after they blocked Jewish settlers ploughing the land with a bulldozer.
PLO officials had said on Monday the standoff at Hebron University ended with agreement to reopen it. The Israeli army later denied a deal was reached and said the closure remained in effect.
"The Israelis have reneged on their commitment to reopen the university," said Diyab al-Sharabati, a Hebron city leader.

The Israeli army, which said it turned back students on Tuesday, had ringed the campus and nearly stormed it on Monday after about 300 students and faculty members broke into the university vowing to resume studies.
The Israeli army said on Tuesday a separate Hebron college, also welded shut in March, was given permission to reopen.
Israel agreed to hand over about 80 percent of Hebron to Palestinian self-rule under a deal signed last year but the long-overdue redeployment has yet to take place.
Palestinians said when Netanyahu was elected in May on a right-wing platform that they considered implementation a test of Israeli Prime Minister Benajamin Netanyahu.

Israeli-PLO talks on the handover are stuck over Israeli demands to change the agreement to provide more security to about 400 militant Jewish settlers who live in Hebron amid more than 100,000 Palestinians.
